question.question: Does a standalone Pure-2D differentiable 5-orbital tight-binding Hamiltonian GNN (TB-EigenGNN) with FP32 eigvalsh and FermiScope readout improve matched 100K development MAE over the retained BondLocal+PairNorm GPTrans-T parent?
question.deficiency: Standard message-passing and Transformer models predict HOMO-LUMO gap as a generic pooled scalar without explicitly diagonalizing a molecular orbital Hamiltonian or enforcing Fermi-level electron counting. Whether a differentiable 5-orbital tight-binding Hamiltonian with exact valence electron FermiScope readout improves 100K gap generalization over BondLocal+PairNorm GPTrans-T is unmeasured.
alternatives: Explicit 5-orbital tight-binding spectral bottleneck loses spatial expressiveness vs 12-layer GPTrans-T
2D tight-binding Hamiltonian underfits without 3D distance modulation
Effect is below the 3 meV material gate
question.positive_decision: Nominate only for candidate-minus-reference selected EMA MAE <= -3.0 meV and paired 95% bootstrap CI upper bound < 0 under strict acceptance; no automatic scale-up.
question.negative_decision: Close this standalone TB-EigenGNN family without hyperparameter grids or automatic retries.

profile.cheapest_falsifier: One same-job 100K 60-pass T4x2 pair comparing retained BondLocal+PairNorm (gptrans.pt) against standalone TB-EigenGNN under identical recipe and split.
